The Lake District: England's Mountain Kingdom

The Lake District is England's largest national park and its most dramatic landscape. Sixteen major lakes, England's highest mountains, and some of the steepest roads in Britain combine to create a motorcycling destination of the highest order. It's also one of the most popular tourist areas in the country, so knowing when and where to ride makes all the difference.

Choosing Your Base

The Lake District is compact but varied. Choose your base based on what you want to ride:

  • Keswick — Northern Lakes. Close to Honister Pass, Newlands, Whinlatter. Good range of pubs, restaurants, and shops
  • Ambleside — Central Lakes. Access to Kirkstone, Wrynose, and Hardknott Passes. Buzzy tourist town with excellent facilities
  • Penrith — Eastern gateway. Close to Ullswater and the A66. Less touristy, good value accommodation
  • Cockermouth — Western Lakes. Quiet base near Buttermere and Ennerdale. Historic market town

The Lakes

Sixteen major lakes, each with its own character. Ullswater is the most beautiful, with the A592 following its shore. Derwentwater near Keswick is the most accessible. Wastwater is the deepest and most dramatic — England's answer to a fjord. Buttermere is small and exquisite, surrounded by fells on all sides.

Beyond the Passes

While the mountain passes are the headline act, the Lake District has much more to offer motorcyclists. The A66 from Penrith to Cockermouth is a fast, flowing road across the northern fells. The A591 from Keswick to Ambleside follows the shores of Thirlmere and Grasmere. The Cumbrian coast from Whitehaven to Barrow is an underrated ride along the Irish Sea.

The Lake District in May or September is a different world from August. The roads are empty, the fells are peaceful, and you remember why this place inspired the Romantic poets.

Biker-Friendly Pubs and Cafes

The Lakes have excellent pub food. The Kirkstone Pass Inn (one of England's highest pubs) is a classic mid-ride stop. The Old Dungeon Ghyll in Langdale is a legendary walkers' and bikers' pub. Moot Hall in Keswick is surrounded by cafes perfect for people-watching over coffee. The Watermill Inn at Ings near Windermere brews its own beer and has a biker-friendly car park.

When to Visit

The Lake District is beautiful year-round but May-June and September-October are the best months for motorcycling. July-August is extremely busy, especially on the passes and around Windermere. Bank holiday weekends should be avoided entirely. Spring brings lambs and wildflowers; autumn brings golden fells and misty mornings.

Practical Tips

Fuel is available in Keswick, Ambleside, Penrith, Windermere, and Cockermouth. There is no fuel on any of the mountain passes. The Lake District has a 40mph speed limit on many roads — respect it. Rain is frequent and the western fells are among the wettest places in England. Carry waterproofs at all times. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in England: A Rider's Guide guide for more. faq.q: Where should I base myself in the Lake District?
faq.a: It depends on what you want to ride. Keswick suits the northern lakes and passes like Honister and Whinlatter, Ambleside gives access to Kirkstone, Wrynose and Hardknott, Penrith is a good-value eastern gateway near Ullswater, and Cockermouth is a quiet western base near Buttermere. The park is compact, so any base works for day rides.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride the Lakes?
faq.a: May-June and September-October are the best months, with quieter roads and peaceful fells. July and August are extremely busy, especially on the passes and around Windermere, and bank holiday weekends should be avoided entirely. Spring brings lambs and wildflowers while autumn brings golden fells and misty mornings.

faq.q: Which pubs and cafes are biker-friendly?
faq.a: The Kirkstone Pass Inn, one of England's highest pubs, is a classic mid-ride stop. The Old Dungeon Ghyll in Langdale is a legendary walkers' and bikers' pub, and the Watermill Inn at Ings near Windermere brews its own beer and has a biker-friendly car park. Keswick's Moot Hall is surrounded by good cafes.

Fuel is available in Keswick, Ambleside, Penrith, Windermere and Cockermouth, but there is no fuel on any of the mountain passes. Fill up in a town before tackling passes like Hardknott and Wrynose, which are steep, narrow and demanding.

faq.q: What should I watch for when riding here?
faq.a: Many Lake District roads carry a 40mph speed limit, so respect it. Rain is frequent and the western fells are among the wettest places in England, so carry waterproofs at all times. The mountain passes are steep with tight hairpins, so ride within your limits, especially in the wet.
